title: How Much Does a Kitchen Fitter Cost UK?
description: How much does a kitchen fitter cost UK? Explore typical labour charges, what fitting includes and the factors that can increase your final quote.
keywords: how much to fit a kitchen
targetKeyword: how much does a kitchen fitter cost uk

blocks.text: If you are budgeting for a new kitchen, one of the first questions is: how much does a kitchen fitter cost in the UK? The answer depends on the size and layout of the room, the condition of the existing services and how much work is involved beyond installing the cabinets. As a rough guide, kitchen fitting labour can range from around £1,500 for a straightforward small installation to £10,000 or more for a complex renovation. These figures are estimates only; every kitchen is different, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.
What is the typical cost of a kitchen fitter in the UK?

For labour only, a kitchen fitter may charge a day rate of roughly £200 to £350, although rates vary by location, experience, the type of work required and whether additional trades are included. A small, uncomplicated kitchen may take several days, while a larger room with new flooring, tiling, plumbing, electrics and bespoke carpentry can take considerably longer.

items: Small or straightforward kitchen installation: roughly £1,500 to £3,000 in labour
Medium kitchen refit with several trades: roughly £3,000 to £6,000 in labour
Large or complex kitchen renovation: around £6,000 to £10,000 or more in labour

A quote may or may not include VAT, waste removal, delivery coordination or specialist items such as worktop fabrication, so it is important to ask what is covered before comparing quotes. A lower headline figure is not necessarily better value if key tasks have been left out.
What does kitchen fitting labour usually include?

A kitchen fitter’s core work normally includes assembling and positioning base and wall units, levelling cabinets, fitting doors and drawers, installing plinths and panels, and fitting worktops where the material and design allow. The installer may also fit sinks, taps, appliances and handles, but these items should be listed clearly in the quotation rather than assumed.

A full kitchen renovation often involves more than cabinet installation. Depending on the project, the labour may also cover removing the old kitchen, preparing walls and floors, adjusting plumbing, installing or altering electrical points, fitting lighting, tiling, decorating and laying flooring. blocks.text: What can increase the final kitchen fitting quote?

The biggest cost difference often comes from the amount of preparation and alteration required. Replacing cabinets in the same positions is generally less labour-intensive than changing the layout. Moving a sink, dishwasher, cooker or radiator can involve alterations to water, waste, gas or electrical connections. If the existing walls or floor are uneven, extra preparation may be needed before cabinets and worktops can be installed accurately.

items: Changing the kitchen layout or removing walls, subject to the appropriate checks
Moving plumbing, drainage, gas supplies or electrical sockets
Upgrading the consumer unit, wiring or lighting arrangements where required
Uneven floors, damaged plaster, damp or poorly prepared walls
Large-format tiles, intricate patterns or extensive wall tiling
Stone, quartz or other worktops needing templates and specialist cutting
Bespoke units, awkward corners, alcoves or limited access to the property
Additional joinery, built-in storage, panelling or finishing work
Working around occupied rooms, restricted parking or difficult material access

blocks.text: How to compare kitchen fitter quotes fairly

Ask each kitchen fitter for an itemised quotation that separates labour, materials, appliances and any subcontracted or specialist work. The quote should describe the number of units, worktop installation, appliance connections, tiling, flooring, decorating, removal of the old kitchen and waste disposal. It should also state whether VAT is included and identify any provisional sums or allowances.

A site visit can be useful because a remote estimate may not reveal access problems, hidden pipework or the condition behind existing cabinets. Before work begins, confirm the expected start date, estimated duration, payment stages, responsibility for ordering materials and what happens if unforeseen work is discovered. If you are planning a more extensive project in the Watford area, you can [request a free, no-obligation quote](/contact) after the scope has been discussed.
Ways to keep kitchen fitting costs under control

Keeping the existing layout is often one of the simplest ways to reduce labour, particularly when the plumbing and electrical points are already suitable. Finalise your cabinet plan, appliance sizes, sink position and worktop choice before installation starts. Last-minute changes can cause delays, additional deliveries and remedial work.

You can also ask whether the fitter can complete several connected tasks as one coordinated project, rather than arranging separate trades yourself. However, do not reduce costs by overlooking essential preparation or using unsuitable materials. Correctly levelling cabinets, sealing worktops and arranging appropriate service connections are important parts of a durable kitchen installation.
Finding the right kitchen fitter

Look for a clear written scope of work, realistic timings and evidence that the installer understands both cabinet fitting and the supporting trades your kitchen needs. faq.q: How much does a kitchen fitter cost per day in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough guide, a kitchen fitter may charge around £200 to £350 per day. Rates vary according to location, experience, project complexity and which additional trades are included. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: How much does it cost to fit a kitchen excluding the units?
faq.a: As a rough guide, labour-only fitting may cost roughly £1,500 to £3,000 for a small straightforward kitchen, rising to £6,000 or more for a larger or more complex renovation. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: Does a kitchen fitter connect appliances?
faq.a: Some fitters include appliance installation or connections, while others charge separately or require specialist trades. Ask for each appliance and connection to be listed in the quotation.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to keep the same kitchen layout?
faq.a: Often, yes. Keeping sinks, appliances and services in their existing positions can reduce plumbing, electrical and preparation work, although the condition of the room still affects the final cost.

faq.q: How long does it take to fit a kitchen?
faq.a: A straightforward installation may take several days, while a full renovation involving plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring and decorating can take considerably longer. Your fitter should provide a project-specific estimate.
